gaps.concept: Natural menopause is diagnosed retrospectively after 12 consecutive months without menses; routine FSH testing is unnecessary in a typical patient over 45.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with hot flashes and amenorrhea asks which test confirms menopause.

gaps.concept: During perimenopause, FSH and estradiol fluctuate; a single normal FSH does not exclude the menopausal transition.
gaps.why_tested: Irregular cycles and hot flashes occur despite a normal hormone result.

gaps.concept: Perimenopausal anovulation eliminates luteal progesterone, causing irregular bleeding and sometimes prolonged estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation.
gaps.why_tested: A patient near menopause develops unpredictable bleeding without a luteal progesterone rise.

gaps.concept: Bilateral oophorectomy causes abrupt surgical menopause; hysterectomy with ovaries retained does not immediately eliminate ovarian hormones.
gaps.why_tested: Symptoms begin immediately after pelvic surgery, and the question asks which organs were removed.

gaps.concept: Primary ovarian insufficiency can include intermittent ovulation and spontaneous pregnancy despite elevated FSH.
gaps.why_tested: A patient under 40 with ovarian insufficiency unexpectedly resumes menses or conceives.

gaps.concept: Estrogen loss reduces vaginal glycogen and lactobacilli, raising vaginal pH; atrophic cytology shows more parabasal cells.
gaps.why_tested: Vaginal dryness accompanies a pH above 5 and predominantly immature epithelial cells.

gaps.concept: Estrogen deficiency increases the RANKL-to-osteoprotegerin ratio, stimulating osteoclast formation and bone resorption.
gaps.why_tested: A postmenopausal osteoporosis question asks for the cellular mechanism of bone loss.

gaps.concept: Postmenopausal osteoporosis produces low bone density, often with normal serum calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase.
gaps.why_tested: A fragility fracture occurs despite normal routine mineral and bone enzyme results.

gaps.concept: Atrophy of the vagina or endometrium is the most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding.
gaps.why_tested: A bleeding vignette asks for the most likely cause after malignancy has been excluded.

gaps.concept: In postmenopausal bleeding, endometrial thickness of 4 mm or less on transvaginal ultrasound makes endometrial cancer unlikely.
gaps.why_tested: An ultrasound thickness is supplied to interpret cancer risk.

gaps.concept: Oral estrogen increases hepatic production of clotting factors; transdermal estrogen has less first-pass hepatic effect and lower VTE risk.
gaps.why_tested: A hormone therapy question compares clot risk between oral and patch formulations.

gaps.concept: Oral estrogen can raise triglycerides and increase cholesterol gallstone risk through hepatic and biliary effects.
gaps.why_tested: Gallstones or hypertriglyceridemia develop after starting oral hormone therapy.

gaps.concept: Low-dose vaginal estrogen treats local genitourinary symptoms but does not adequately treat hot flashes; it generally requires no progestin.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with an intact uterus needs treatment for vaginal dryness alone versus systemic vasomotor symptoms.

gaps.concept: Systemic estrogen limits menopausal bone loss but is not prescribed solely to prevent cardiovascular disease or other chronic conditions.
gaps.why_tested: A patient without vasomotor symptoms requests hormone therapy for long-term disease prevention.

gaps.concept: For primary ovarian insufficiency, estrogen replacement is generally continued until the usual age of menopause if no contraindication exists.
gaps.why_tested: A young patient with ovarian insufficiency needs a treatment choice despite concerns drawn from older postmenopausal cohorts.

gaps.concept: Cyclic estrogen-progestin therapy causes predictable withdrawal bleeding; continuous combined therapy aims for amenorrhea after initial spotting.
gaps.why_tested: Bleeding patterns differ between two hormone therapy schedules.

gaps.concept: Raloxifene acts as an estrogen agonist in bone and antagonist in breast; it can worsen hot flashes and increase VTE risk.
gaps.why_tested: An osteoporosis drug is considered for a postmenopausal patient with vasomotor symptoms or clot risk.

gaps.concept: Paroxetine inhibits CYP2D6 and can reduce conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite.
gaps.why_tested: A breast cancer survivor taking tamoxifen needs a nonhormonal treatment for hot flashes.
